title: improve-streaming-backpressure-kernel-pacing-and-flush-cadence
author: Maya R. Patel
description: Motivation: production streaming customers saw 95th/99th token latency spikes when model sequence interleaving and kernel dispatch jitter aligned under high concurrency. Root causes identified: the token emission loop was flushing per-request too aggressively, kernel selection introduced micro-scheduling stalls on heterogenous sequences, and continuous-batching queues lacked a backpressure signal tied to active KV cache memory pressure. This PR addresses these by (1) introducing an adaptive flush cadence that groups sub-token flushes into a short window to amortize syscalls and network writes while preserving low tail latency for first tokens, (2) adding a soft backpressure token to the continuous-batcher that temporarily reduces per-request batching depth when KV cache hit-rate drops or memory pressure rises, (3) pacing kernel dispatch for mixed sequence lengths via a simple cost-estimator in the kernel selector to avoid dispatching long-seq kernels immediately ahead of short-seq work, and (4) minor refactors to the token loop to separate emission, checkpointing, and stall-detection logic. Implementation summary: streamer.cpp now tracks per-stream last-flush timestamp and an adaptive_window_ms computed from recent per-token latency percentiles; a new flush_coalescer module consolidates writes within the window. continuous_batcher adds a backpressure_count that increments when kv_cache_manager reports degraded hit_rate or memory_watermark>0.8; when backpressure_count>threshold, the batcher lowers max_batch_size and exposes a diagnostics metric. kernel_selector computes a normalized cost metric (compute_tokens*cost_factor + io_penalty) and delays high-cost kernels by small randomized jitter to reduce head-of-line blocking. Observability: added metrics streaming.flush_coalesce_ratio, batcher.backpressure_level, kernel.pacing_delay and tagged spans for flush-window boundary events. Tests and benchmarks: synthetic microbenchmarks show 95th token latency reduction of 18-32% across r4 and a100 instances for mixed-long/short workloads, and overall token throughput maintained within 2% of baseline. Safety and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.streaming.adaptive_flush=true and batcher backpressure disabled by default. Rollout plan: enable in canary for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor streaming.flush_coalesce_ratio and tail-token SLOs and KV cache hit_rate; automatic rollback if 95th latency regresses >5%. Notes: this is performance-sensitive; code paths touched are hot and extra attention paid to allocations and atomic operations. See release_notes for user-facing changes and observability additions.
commits: refactor(streamer): split flush coalescer and emission loop
perf(batcher): add backpressure_count and diagnostics metric
perf(kernel): introduce cost estimator and pacing jitter
kvcache: expose hit_rate and memory_watermark to batcher
docs: add observability section for streaming metrics
tests: add streaming latency microbenchmarks and integration test
review_comments: Alec Zhou: Please add a microbenchmark comparing fixed flush cadences vs adaptive_window_ms; we need a reproducible script. Author reply: added tests/benchmarks/streaming_latency.py with parameters and CI entry.

Priya Menon: Concerned about atomics in hot path; can we avoid extra CAS in streamer? Author reply: changed to read-mostly atomic with seqlock fallback for updates, moved cost computation off critical path.

Diego Ramirez: Suggest exposing the backpressure signal in the SDK / control-plane so ops can opt to drain queues; minor nit about metric labels. Author reply: exposed batcher.backpressure_level as numeric gauge and added tags runtime.instance_id and model.name per Diego's suggestion.
Alec Zhou: CI flake on macOS test harness unrelated; reran and all green. Approve after small logging cleanup.
Priya Menon: Approved. Diego Ramirez: Approved.
release_notes: - Reduced streaming token 95th latency by 18-32% for mixed-sequence workloads via adaptive flush coalescing and kernel pacing. - Added runtime flags: runtime.streaming.adaptive_flush and runtime.batcher.enable_backpressure. - New observability metrics: streaming.flush_coalesce_ratio, batcher.backpressure_level, kernel.pacing_delay.
